hey everybody this is going to be a short video 
for me so grain of salt a little over a week ago

to celebrate the game's pending launch I put out 
a top five multi-class builds video for Baldur's

Gate 3 as you probably know and though I figured 
it would do well you guys kind of blew me away

with the response here it quickly became my most 
viewed video ever rip blade singer 2.0 you had

a good run and it doesn't seem to be slowing down 
at all so thank you for that you guys are freaking

awesome now I am currently working on doing a 
more favorite multi-class builds for Baldur's

Gate 3 video that should be out next week but in 
the meantime I wanted to give a quick update to

that first video as you probably know in order to 
get the video out by the time the game released I

had to write the script and record and edit that 
video before the game actually released I talked

about that in the video but yeah that meant 
that I was going to sometimes be making some

assumptions and would inevitably be wrong on some 
things once we got the full version of the game

and not surprisingly that proved to be true so I 
wanted to quickly here put out a video that simply

updates some things from that video based on the 
full release version of the game that we have in

our hands and man is it a great game right so 
fun okay so as for the first build the holy

Warrior there's really really only one big thing 
to note but it is a big one and it's that larion

has changed the Berserker Barbarian so that when 
you go into your frenzied rage yes you do get to

make a bonus action attack each round but every 
time you do it lowers your chance to hit by one

on all attacks and that is brutal honestly I'd 
almost rather have a level of exhaustion like you

get in 5e so yeah that means you kind of almost 
never want to use that bonus action attack unless

you're really desperate to finish off an enemy 
or something and that is too bad you do get the

ability to make an improvised weapon attack 
as a bonus action that does not suffer that

same penalty and that improvised weapon can even 
potentially be another creature and you can even

throw them so there's still some really cool stuff 
going on with Berserker Barbarian and in general

I still do really like Barbarian with Paladin but 
mostly for the rage and The Reckless attack with

this change I think I'd probably end up taking a 
different sub subclass on my Barbarian probably

wildheart would be my go-to or maybe even just 
stop at two levels of Barbarian if we did that

instead of being a Berserker then you'd want to 
get the pole arm Master Fee so that you can get

a bonus action attack still and switch to using a 
glaive or a Halbert instead of like a great sword

or a maul or a great ax right and here's something 
that I'm not seeing a lot of other people making

Baldur's Gate 3 content talk about when they are 
discussing Feats it seems like everybody is saying

yeah pull on Master great feat it gives you an 
opportunity attack when someone enters your reach

and you get a bonus action attack with the like 
blunt end the butt of the pole arm but it's only

a D4 of damage so this really not that great 
and here's something those of you new to DND

rules should know the damage die of your weapon is 
actually not all that important most of the damage

that you do in DND and Baldur's Gate 3 as a weapon 
user tends to come from things that you do to

add damage to your attacks your ability modifiers 
your rage damage spells like pecs or Hunter's Mark

and above all things damage from a feat-like great 
weapon Master which adds 10 damage to your attack

if you hit with a heavy weapon and glaves and 
halberds are heavy weapons so sure the butt of

your halberd only hits for a D4 but when you're 
adding three or four for strength two for rage

and ten for great weapon master who cares the 
most important thing is that you get an attack

with that weapon now one important note at the 
time of this recording pull-on Master does not

seem to be working properly in Baldur's Gate 3. 
I've tested it myself I've seen a lot of people

talking about this online but long story short it 
seems to not always correctly be adding all of the

sources of damage that you should be getting on 
that bonus action butt of the pole arm attack I

have to assume that larion is going to be fixing 
this hopefully very soon maybe even by the time

this video comes out if they haven't help me 
be a squeaky wheel here and see if they can

get a patch in quick anyway yeah this sucks 
because it means you need to invest another

feat now into Polar Master right so maybe you do 
go Barbarian four still so you can end the game

with three Feats by level 12. it's a bummer but 
frenzied rage was probably overpowered in Early

Access so I'm not all that surprised to be honest 
to see them Nerf it a bit I just think they might

have gone a little too hard with the Nerf bat for 
build number two the ninja a couple of Errata one

I had read that you were going to start out with 
a D6 of damage to your unarmed strikes instead

it stays at D4 like in 5e but then it scales more 
quickly than it does in 5e so you go to a D6 for

your unarm strike at level three of Monk and then 
a d8 at level six also I was assuming that Shadow

Monks got Shadow strike at level six but it's 
actually not until Level 11. considering that

and seeing the way of the open hand in its full 
release Glory I think I'm personally gonna change

my character that I'm playing with this build in 
my initial playthrough to be an open hand monk

they get to knock an enemy prone with their Flurry 
of Blows among other things and since in Baldur's

Gate 3 you can Flurry of Blows before you take 
the attack action unlike in 5e that means you

can potentially knock the enemy prone right at the 
beginning of your turn and then enjoy advantage on

a prone enemy right for all of the rest of your 
attacks that round it's a little less ninja-like

and Shadow monk would still work great but 
mechanically I think open hand has the upper hand

now you may be thinking wait a second we were an 
Assassin Rogue we already got advantage on our

first round of combat so knocking an enemy prone 
isn't all that important for us for this build

and that kind of leads me to another thing that 
I wanted to mention I got a lot of comments from

people on that video saying that I was clearly 
mistaken for taking assassin as thiefrogues are

much better since they get an extra bonus action 
every single turn I'll admit that I was skeptical

that you would be able to just use that bonus 
action for whatever you wanted once the game

launched surely they would limit it to only making 
like one bonus action attack per turn if you could

make an attack with your bonus action but as of 
this recording at least they have not nerfed it

that means that if you wanted to and had the 
key for it you could Flurry of Blows twice on

your turn for four attacks with just your bonus 
actions and that's kind of crazy I feel like I

could do a whole video on the best ways to abuse 
Thief Rogue in botherscape maybe I will but that

said I still don't think it's necessarily the 
best rogue subclass for our ninja it kind of

all depends on what you want to do with your 
character my goal was to make a sneaky burst

damage dealer who could just flat out kill one 
or two Targets at the beginning of combat with

surprise in that case you actually do get more 
damage from automatic Critical Hits on 4 attacks

when one of them includes sneak attack damage 
especially since that damage is doubled on a

crit as well then you would from six non-critical 
attacks if you spent two key points to Flurry of

Blows twice as a thief on that opening round 
right of course you are burning through your

resources more quickly in that scenario but yeah 
your sustained damage over the rest of the fight

would be higher as a thief even if you didn't 
have the key since you could always then make

two unarmed strikes even without key points by 
using two bonus actions right you don't need

Flurry of Blows to make two unarmed strikes in 
that scenario but yeah burst damage is incredibly

valuable in this game taking out an enemy or two 
right at the beginning of the fight so they don't

even get a chance to attack you and your friends 
might actually do more to help you win the fight

than doing more damage on round two and three and 
four right anyway know your options and build the

way that's best for what you want to do right 
I said this was going to be a short video yeah

I don't think I have any changes or updates to 
build number three the ultimate support or build

number four the ultimate Blaster both of those 
seem to be working as we thought they would for

build number five though the ultimate tank a lot 
of you also commented to say that alas you cannot

actually rage while in Bear form and it's true and 
that sucks but what you may not know is that you

can rage first then wild shape and if you do you 
get to keep your rage all right so it kind of just

changes the order in which we do things not so 
bad that said yeah when you wild shape it pretty

much replaces your pop bar right and you're pretty 
much limited to just do the things that that wild

shaped bear can do which is a real bummer and I 
really hope that larion fixes that at some point

in the future okay I think that's it if I missed 
anything else in that first video that didn't get

mentioned here please let me know in the comments 
otherwise I love you guys thank you for all of

your support and watch for that second bg3 builds 
video coming out next Tuesday okay take care
